comparison: Both address claims C8, C9, C51 regarding ARM noise effects. OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED based on statistical analysis showing no stress effects. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, raising major concerns about untested ultrasonic frequencies (20-110 kHz) that could affect rodents, noting the study only tested audible noise.

Both address claims C16-C19, C61-C64 regarding ARM validation in pain models. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence and catch trial controls. Peer review affirms the system is well validated with claims well supported by experimental evidence.

Both address claims C20-C23 regarding experimenter effects on habituation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence from two-way ANOVA. Peer review affirms these findings demonstrate important experimenter effects that the ARM can circumvent.

Both address claims C29-C31, C65-C66 regarding differential effects of stimulus intensity on reflexive vs affective features. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes linear regression analysis. Peer review affirms these provide compelling evidence for standardizing manual stimulus applications.

Both address claims C56-C60 regarding force sensor innovation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes technical capabilities validated through pain model experiments. Peer review affirms new additions have been methodically tested for reproducibility and reliability.

Both address claims C24-C28 regarding experimenter-dependent and sex-dependent effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical evidence across multiple researchers. Peer review affirms proof of concept studies showing how the system reveals experimenter effects on behavior, with C44 not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on claims C42, C46-C50 regarding technical design. OpenEval R1 also includes C6-C7 (targeting accuracy). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval combines design specifications with performance data. Peer review R15 affirms technical design without concerns, noting the system is well validated.

Both address claims C6-C7 regarding improved targeting accuracy and consistency. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R1 includes additional technical claims (C42, C46-C50). Peer review explicitly affirms ARM reduces variability with clear examples contrasting experimenter vs ARM stimulus application.

Both address claims C10-C12 regarding force application accuracy and temporal consistency. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 also includes C13-C15. Peer review affirms these findings, noting outstanding job of rigorous quantitative comparison and clear, convincing presentation.

Both address claims C14-C15 regarding elimination of inter-researcher variability. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 groups these with C10-C13 on performance metrics. Peer review R5 focuses specifically on C14-C15, affirming ARM's ability to eliminate experimenter variability.

Both address claim C13 regarding speed improvements. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 groups C13 with other performance metrics (C10-C15). Peer review R4 focuses on C13, affirming ARM's efficiency advantages in quickly oscillating between stimuli.

Both address claims C52-C53 regarding lower-cost camera validation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R9 also includes C54-C55 on software improvements. Peer review affirms new additions have been methodically tested for reproducibility and reliability.

Both address claims C54-C55 regarding software improvements and integration. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R9 also includes C52-C53 on camera validation. Peer review affirms system integrates well with automated analysis programs for complete standardization package.

Both address claims C32-C34 regarding neural response detection. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 includes additional claims (C35-C38, C45, C67-C68) on neural-behavioral correlations. Peer review R10 affirms ARM can be used with in vivo imaging techniques.

Both address claims C35-C38 regarding neural-behavioral correlations. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R8 includes additional claims (C32-C34, C45, C67-C68). Peer review R11 affirms successful integration without methodological concerns, noting methodical testing for reproducibility.

OpenEval R11 addresses claims C1-C5, C39-C41, C70 regarding background literature and scientific rationale. Rated SUPPORTED as appropriately cited prior work establishing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C69, C71-C72 regarding broader impact and accessibility. Rated UNCERTAIN as these represent aspirational goals rather than demonstrated outcomes. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these interpretive claims.

OpenEval R13 addresses claims C73-C89 regarding methods, procedures, and regulatory compliance. Rated SUPPORTED as factual methodological descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological details.
